page: Microsoft Azure E128-32as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Easv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 32 dedicated vCPUs, consisting of 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The server is equipped with an extensive 1024.0 GB of RAM, yielding a massive 32.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the E128-32as_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU, single-threaded gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 10%. Multi-threaded performance is also strong, with bzip3 decompression and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the top 25%. However, multi-core stress-ng performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into the average range. For LLM inference, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds on small 135M models but exhibits poor performance in the bottom 10% when generating text with large 70B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance provides high resource density for memory-bound workloads, offering a massive memory footprint relative to its 32 vCPUs. This makes it highly suitable for large in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications requiring substantial RAM without the cost of additional CPU cores. The lack of local storage means external storage performance must be factored in. Recommended workloads include memory-intensive database operations, large-scale data caching, and memory-heavy enterprise applications.
